Comeback Noni

By: Sophia Phirippides | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
In the new year, South Africa’s own World Boxing Champion Noni Tenge is scheduled to defend her WBF title in Las Vegas. But Noni’s comeback trail has been a long trek in the wilderness.

Unique Selling Point:
Noni Tenge is one of the country's World Champion Sports Stars. But not only is she a World Boxing Champion, Noni is the holder of a Sports Management Diploma. Well, she would have the Diploma if the Minister of Sport would pay the last grant installments promised to her. Why is Noni so undervalued by South Africa?

Summary:
South African Noni Tenge is World Boxing Champion - "She Be Stinging”. Her alias is in homage to Muhammed Ali - he who "floats like a butterfly, stings like a bee".
In contrast to Ali, Noni, winner of no less than 5 different World Titles, as a South African female boxer is battling in the wilderness. She struggles to fund trips to her fights, which has cost her two of her titles. Noni has even had her government-funded educational diploma withheld because government has not paid the final installment. Despite women’s boxing only gaining broad acceptance in the 21st century, in other sports or in other countries, Noni Tenge would be a superstar sports woman and would not be living in her current flat-sharing accommodation.
The winner of eight world title fights and with only one loss to her name, Noni is from the Eastern Cape. In 2011, Noni became the first female fighter to win the IBF Welterweight crown. Born in East London, known to the world as South Africa’s boxing capital, Noni Tenge debuted professionally in 2007 and has an outstanding record of eighteen wins, one defeat and a single draw from twenty outings (11 of her wins being by Knock Out). She is truly world class.
Noni was one of five women boxers who put on an exhibition for parliament, at the invitation of President Mbeki, which inspired government to legalize female boxing in 2001. However, seventeen years on, women boxers are struggling to have sustainable careers, with a lack of government support for even a champion like Noni, South Africa’s undisputed number one woman fighter.
As she prepares for her next World Title fight, we interview Noni and witness her current training and living conditions. And as Noni continues to wait for the certificate confirming her successfully completed sports management diploma, we ask the Minister of Sport, Thokozile Xasa, why her department has withheld the final payments for Noni’s education.

Further information:
In January 2019, Noni Tenge will make a mandatory defense of her WBF Super Welterweight world title, following a short time away from the boxing ring. For the last year, with government funding unforthcoming, Noni has been working as part of an anti-poaching unit. Literally and figuratively, government has left her in the wilderness. Not only that, under Fikile Mbalula, the Ministry of Sport granted funding for Noni’s education at Walter Sisulu University for a Sports Management Diploma, but at the last moment failed to pay the final installments which are required so that she can receive her certificate.
We interview Nicky Erasmus, the boxing coach who facilitated Noni in getting the anti-poaching work and who currently trains Noni. We confront Minister of Sport, Thokozile Xasa, to find out why Noni has not received final funding for her studies and to question her about the current state of women’s boxing in South Africa.
In the ring, Noni Tenge has earned the alias ‘She Bee Stinging’, but away from the ring Noni prioritizes her influence on young South African women. She wishes to be a role model to inspire South African’s to pursue sport and boxing in particular, to be strong in the face of the high rates of crimes against women in South Africa. In her own words, “I hope I can inspire more women and young people to believe in themselves and to follow their dreams of becoming a world success. No matter your upbringing or your circumstances, one can overcome these obstacles and become the best in the world, I have, so anyone can do it.”
We interview Howard Goldberg, President of the World Boxing Federation, who verifies Noni’s achievements as a champion boxer and as an ambassador of the sport. Both Nicky Erasmus and Howard Goldberg can attest to how Noni has also been let down by unscrupulous boxing promoters throughout her boxing career.
We film Noni in training, in and out of the ring, to get an intimate view of what it takes to get to the top of her sport again. After the funding let-downs, Noni has been given this come back opportunity from a number of sympathetic parties. Previously, Noni had been sponsored a Mini Cooper, but with no funding available it was left standing unmaintained. Her trainers are now repairing the car and helping Noni get her driver’s license. She should soon have the freedom of movement a car provides and that she so badly needs. A local gym are providing Noni with free access to their training facilities. Winston Wilson is Noni’s new manager, fighting in Noni’s corner.

Press Release:


World Boxing Champion Noni Tenge one of South Africa’s most decorated athletes, needs to fight again to stay in the game. What became of her government funding? With new management there’s hope on the horizon and Noni is scheduled to defend her WBF title in America in 2019.

Script:


Shots of Noni on punching bag

Noni: It’s not easy to become a female boxer in SA.

Shots of Noni on the “boxing goody” slow mo

Noni: I decided to stand up for myself

Shots of Noni skipping

Noni: I’m very committed

Shots of Noni running on the beach slowmo

Noni: If I’m losing we’re all losing

Noni: Women were not allowed to box in SA until the former president Thabo Mbeki gave us a chance to fight for ourselves.

LINK: She is one of 5 women who motivated government to legalise female boxing in SA in 2001. She has won 5 different world titles in various weight divisions. Have you heard of Noni Tenge? She be stinging

Noni: It is very hard. I'm doing it because I love it because i love the game but when it comes to the money side its very difficult because i don’t have money, i don't have anything.

VO: At the age of 37, Noni holds the Women’s WBF Super Welterweight title. Howard Goldberg is president of the WBF and also assists young boxers to gain access to the sport.

Howard: Noni is an icon in SA boxing. Noni is women's boxing in SA. She is a hero to not only the women fighters coming through today but all fighters.

VO: She grew up in the rural outskirts of East London, in the Eastern Cape.

Noni: I started boxing at an early age, I grew up in a boxing family. My eldest brother was a boxer.
Howard: She came from a very difficult background, the men didn’t accept a woman fighting at that time but Noni grew, she was strong she trained with the guys.

VO: Noni debuted professionally in 2007 and has an outstanding record of 18 wins, one defeat and a single draw, 10 of her wins by knockout.

Noni: The fight was on the 12th of September 2017, I was defending my title against Mapuleng Ngubane

VO: Her achievements beat the odds given her often limited resources.

Noni: I didn’t get any sponsors, I didn’t have money to buy vegetables I didn’t have money to buy the sport drinks and supplements, I have to wait for the fight to get the money. If I don’t fight I can’t get the money.

VO: Support came Noni’s way from 2011, when the Department of Sport and Recreation, under then Minister Fikile Mbalula, sponsored Noni’s diploma in Sports management at Walter Sisulu University, facilitated a sponsored car and one year’s living expenses. It looked like Noni’s career was all set, until in 2016 the funding suddenly stopped.

Noni: After that i never had any support. I feel like they failed me

VO: Noni graduated but discovered that her final year’s fees had not been paid by the department and her qualification was withheld.

Noni: I asked them if they can pay the fees the lady who was responsible that she was on the athlete support side then she said Noni i will have to speak to the office because minister is aware of you. I decided to quit because i have to buy the airtime myself.

LINK: Forced to find work and without her diploma in hand Noni had to sideline her pursuit of more world titles and she joined an anti abalone poaching unit here in the Eastern Cape just to survive

Russie: She was part of the anti poaching team. She was a toughie then.

VO: Nicky Erasmus the co-owner of Dark Water Ops and a boxing coach, took Noni under his wing hoping to train her while she worked to support herself.

Rassie: Because of the work she does in the anti poaching her boxing went a bit backwards because of the hours she couldn’t get to gym

Howard: She would be getting mega fights overseas. She had a mega fight lined up. It fell through for a variety of reasons.

VO: In boxing, if a champion doesn’t defend their title within a year, it gets stripped. For Noni the periods between bouts became too long.

Noni: The IBF title had been stripped because i was inactive for a year. You can’t defend your title if you can’t get any challenger and boxing is about the promoter.

Howard: Who let Noni down? There was so many contributing factors; lack of funds, promoters, lack of fights, cancellations, yet Noni remains rated almost at the top of her weight group in the world.

VO: Noni’s star was destined to shine, and her coach Rassie had to find a solution, that’s when he approached Grant Austin the owner of Edge fitness, a high tech gym in Port Elizabeth.

Grant: I think the light bulb moment for me was the day she came here with all her belts. It blew my mind. You actually understand that you're in the presence of greatness.

Rassie: Overseas people get sponsored they don’t go anywhere but the gym that’s why i went to grant and tried to see if we can’t give that to Noni in SA.

Mac: what were some things that made you think i've gotta help her and make you want to help her

Grant: she's got a very compelling story. She should be an absolute rockstar and she's had a lot of challenges so we thought if we can bring her onto our team and help her get to where she wants to be that was our objective

VO: So Grant, a gym owner who has never ventured into the world of boxing, took on the challenge and now Noni has three conditioning coaches and a new manager, Winston Wilson.

Winston: We were trying to resurrect her career, a client like Noni doesn’t land on your doorstep a 5 time world champ. Its nurtured from a teenager and that manager will stay with her which is the norm, but in this case things haven’t gone the way they should have gone

VO: In South African sport government support is key to the success of an athlete and somewhere along the line communication broke down between the Department of Sport and Noni.

Winston: I've sent emails to the department of sport just to ask for support for Noni. I've tried endlessly, there's no responses.They know who Noni is, she's an ambassador for the sport, you can’t ignore who she is.

VO: We approached the Department of Sport and Recreation, and were met by Director General Alec Moemi and CEO of Boxing South Africa, Tsholofelo Lejaka.

DDG: Noni is one of our star boxers. She has been a trailblazer for us as government and department of sport. We have been providing support over the years to her.

Tsholo: Noni is a rare breed, over and above her talents in the ring she's one of the most articulate, charismatic and well educated boxers.

LINK: With all of these accolades in some countries Noni would be a superstar sports woman. She wouldn’t be living in shared accommodation and struggling to pay rent and constantly fighting to save her boxing career

Howard: Noni would certainly make a living in the United States. The fighter who she was supposed to fight this year Clarissa Shields who’s a 2 time olympic winner, she's earning a million dollars a fight

Mac: One of the things she's spoken about is she hasn’t had support from the department. Could more have been done to help Noni

DDG: Our department finds itself in a difficult financial scenario there are budget cuts, there is room for improvement and support of our athletes including Noni.

VO: The matter of Noni’s final year University fees of
R37 730 still needed settling.

Mac: The issue that we're looking at is her fees not being paid for her diploma. Is there a commitment from your side that this will be resolved.

DDG: We require that we are given the necessary records from the university, a responsibility that lies with the athlete.

Mac: So we get the documents you pay

DDG: Certainly no issue.

VO: The Department together with Boxing SA were somewhat floored to hear that Noni had been struggling and feels unsupported by them. They undertook to resuscitate the relationship.

Tsholo: We will give her the type of support that a legend in the making of her type does deserve.

DDG: Right now her career has not ended therefore women in boxing program will be most appropriate to support herand we are looking at engaging with her and her new management.

Winston: We need government backing that government can get behind, here’s infrastructure we can build the gyms, bring young kids through and the eastern cape can become a hub for boxing like it was known to be.

Noni: In 5 years or 6 years I will be developing young boxers of south africa to join boxing more especially the women.

VO: Noni is on the comeback trail, zoning in on the defence of her WBF title this year.

Grant: She can spend a lot of her time exercising and training, when before she had to earn money, worry about her training, worry about getting to gym, gym fees, food, basic necessities, It’s obviously a lot better for her now.

Howard: We're looking at doing the fight not only for the WBF but for 2 or 3 of the other major bodies. A mega fight and she'll be the main fight showtime united states

Mac: Are you ready

Noni: Ready

Mac: You'll see with me as well

Noni: Are you going to box with me? Are you sure?


Boxing match begins

LINK: South Africa you don't want to get into the ring with this woman. I am absolutely pummeled. I've just been in the ring with her for 10 minutes, her strength, her power, determination is absolutely amazing. Now we all know why she's called she bee stinging. Look out for her, she's got her next world title coming up, we've got to go out there and support her. Thank you Noni

VO: Noni’s star was destined to shine, and her coach Rassie had to find a solution, that’s when he approached Grant Austin the owner of Edge fitness, a high tech gym in Port Elizabeth. Grant: I think the light bulb moment for me was the day she came here with all her belts. It blew my mind. You actually understand that you're in the presence of greatness. Rassie: Overseas people get sponsored they don’t go anywhere but the gym that’s why i went to grant and tried to see if we can’t give that to Noni in SA. Mac: what were some things that made you think i've gotta help her and make you want to help her Grant: she's got a very compelling story. She should be an absolute rockstar and she's had a lot of challenges so we thought if we can bring her onto our team and help her get to where she wants to be that was our objective VO: So Grant, a gym owner who has never ventured into the world of boxing, took on the challenge and now Noni has three conditioning coaches and a new manager, Winston Wilson. Winston: We were trying to resurrect her career, a client like Noni doesn’t land on your doorstep a 5 time world champ. Its nurtured from a teenager and that manager will stay with her which is the norm, but in this case things haven’t gone the way they should have gone VO: In South African sport government support is key to the success of an athlete and somewhere along the line communication broke down between the Department of Sport and Noni. Winston: I've sent emails to the department of sport just to ask for support for Noni. I've tried endlessly, there's no responses.They know who Noni is, she's an ambassador for the sport, you can’t ignore who she is. VO: We approached the Department of Sport and Recreation, and were met by Director General Alec Moemi and CEO of Boxing South Africa, Tsholofelo Lejaka. DDG: Noni is one of our star boxers. She has been a trailblazer for us as government and department of sport. We have been providing support over the years to her. Tsholo: Noni is a rare breed, over and above her talents in the ring she's one of the most articulate, charismatic and well educated boxers. LINK: With all of these accolades in some countries Noni would be a superstar sports woman. She wouldn’t be living in shared accommodation and struggling to pay rent and constantly fighting to save her boxing career Howard: Noni would certainly make a living in the United States. The fighter who she was supposed to fight this year Clarissa Shields who’s a 2 time olympic winner, she's earning a million dollars a fight Mac: One of the things she's spoken about is she hasn’t had support from the department. Could more have been done to help Noni DDG: Our department finds itself in a difficult financial scenario there are budget cuts, there is room for improvement and support of our athletes including Noni. VO: The matter of Noni’s final year University fees of R37 730 still needed settling. Mac: The issue that we're looking at is her fees not being paid for her diploma. Is there a commitment from your side that this will be resolved. DDG: We require that we are given the necessary records from the university, a responsibility that lies with the athlete. Mac: So we get the documents you pay DDG: Certainly no issue. VO: The Department together with Boxing SA were somewhat floored to hear that Noni had been struggling and feels unsupported by them. They undertook to resuscitate the relationship. Tsholo: We will give her the type of support that a legend in the making of her type does deserve. DDG: Right now her career has not ended therefore women in boxing program will be most appropriate to support herand we are looking at engaging with her and her new management. Winston: We need government backing that government can get behind, here’s infrastructure we can build the gyms, bring young kids through and the eastern cape can become a hub for boxing like it was known to be. Noni: In 5 years or 6 years I will be developing young boxers of south africa to join boxing more especially the women. VO: Noni is on the comeback trail, zoning in on the defence of her WBF title this year. Grant: She can spend a lot of her time exercising and training, when before she had to earn money, worry about her training, worry about getting to gym, gym fees, food, basic necessities, It’s obviously a lot better for her now. Howard: We're looking at doing the fight not only for the WBF but for 2 or 3 of the other major bodies. A mega fight and she'll be the main fight showtime united states Mac: Are you ready Noni: Ready Mac: You'll see with me as well Noni: Are you going to box with me? Are you sure? Boxing match begins LINK: South Africa you don't want to get into the ring with this woman. I am absolutely pummeled. I've just been in the ring with her for 10 minutes, her strength, her power, determination is absolutely amazing. Now we all know why she's called she bee stinging. Look out for her, she's got her next world title coming up, we've got to go out there and support her. Thank you Noni

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): In the new year, South Africa’s own World Boxing Champion Noni Tenge is scheduled to defend her WBF title in Las Vegas. But Noni’s comeback trail has been a long trek in the wilderness.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Noni Tenge is one of the country's World Champion Sports Stars. But not only is she a World Boxing Champion, Noni is the holder of a Sports Management Diploma. Well, she would have the Diploma if the Minister of Sport would pay the last grant installments promised to her. Why is Noni so undervalued by South Africa?
metadata.Summary: South African Noni Tenge is World Boxing Champion - "She Be Stinging”. Her alias is in homage to Muhammed Ali - he who "floats like a butterfly, stings like a bee". In contrast to Ali, Noni, winner of no less than 5 different World Titles, as a South African female boxer is battling in the wilderness. She struggles to fund trips to her fights, which has cost her two of her titles. Noni has even had her government-funded educational diploma withheld because government has not paid the final installment. Despite women’s boxing only gaining broad acceptance in the 21st century, in other sports or in other countries, Noni Tenge would be a superstar sports woman and would not be living in her current flat-sharing accommodation. The winner of eight world title fights and with only one loss to her name, Noni is from the Eastern Cape. In 2011, Noni became the first female fighter to win the IBF Welterweight crown. Born in East London, known to the world as South Africa’s boxing capital, Noni Tenge debuted professionally in 2007 and has an outstanding record of eighteen wins, one defeat and a single draw from twenty outings (11 of her wins being by Knock Out). She is truly world class. Noni was one of five women boxers who put on an exhibition for parliament, at the invitation of President Mbeki, which inspired government to legalize female boxing in 2001. However, seventeen years on, women boxers are struggling to have sustainable careers, with a lack of government support for even a champion like Noni, South Africa’s undisputed number one woman fighter. As she prepares for her next World Title fight, we interview Noni and witness her current training and living conditions. And as Noni continues to wait for the certificate confirming her successfully completed sports management diploma, we ask the Minister of Sport, Thokozile Xasa, why her department has withheld the final payments for Noni’s education.
metadata.Further information: In January 2019, Noni Tenge will make a mandatory defense of her WBF Super Welterweight world title, following a short time away from the boxing ring. For the last year, with government funding unforthcoming, Noni has been working as part of an anti-poaching unit. Literally and figuratively, government has left her in the wilderness. Not only that, under Fikile Mbalula, the Ministry of Sport granted funding for Noni’s education at Walter Sisulu University for a Sports Management Diploma, but at the last moment failed to pay the final installments which are required so that she can receive her certificate. We interview Nicky Erasmus, the boxing coach who facilitated Noni in getting the anti-poaching work and who currently trains Noni. We confront Minister of Sport, Thokozile Xasa, to find out why Noni has not received final funding for her studies and to question her about the current state of women’s boxing in South Africa. In the ring, Noni Tenge has earned the alias ‘She Bee Stinging’, but away from the ring Noni prioritizes her influence on young South African women. She wishes to be a role model to inspire South African’s to pursue sport and boxing in particular, to be strong in the face of the high rates of crimes against women in South Africa. In her own words, “I hope I can inspire more women and young people to believe in themselves and to follow their dreams of becoming a world success. No matter your upbringing or your circumstances, one can overcome these obstacles and become the best in the world, I have, so anyone can do it.” We interview Howard Goldberg, President of the World Boxing Federation, who verifies Noni’s achievements as a champion boxer and as an ambassador of the sport. Both Nicky Erasmus and Howard Goldberg can attest to how Noni has also been let down by unscrupulous boxing promoters throughout her boxing career. We film Noni in training, in and out of the ring, to get an intimate view of what it takes to get to the top of her sport again. After the funding let-downs, Noni has been given this come back opportunity from a number of sympathetic parties. Previously, Noni had been sponsored a Mini Cooper, but with no funding available it was left standing unmaintained. Her trainers are now repairing the car and helping Noni get her driver’s license. She should soon have the freedom of movement a car provides and that she so badly needs. A local gym are providing Noni with free access to their training facilities. Winston Wilson is Noni’s new manager, fighting in Noni’s corner.
